nodes.name: Fetch YC Directory
nodes.notes: About 10MB. Read as text and parsed downstream: the body is a top-level JSON array, and letting n8n parse it produces 6000 items instead of one. neverError is off here - an empty directory is not a run worth continuing.

nodes.notes: No API key and no rate limit worth the name. neverError: HN being down must not cost the YC half of the run.

nodes.notes: Item 0 does not exist, which is the deliberate outcome when Pick HN Thread found no thread: a 404 with neverError on, an empty children array, and a YC-only run.

nodes.notes: The thesis, in two regular expressions: reject anyone advertising an infrastructure role, keep anyone advertising engineering roles without one.

parameters.query:
-- Record every candidate this run decided about, and insert the ones that
-- became companies. One statement, because a company inserted without its
-- discovery_seen row would be re-evaluated every morning forever, and a
-- discovery_seen row written without its company would lose the candidate
-- permanently.
--
-- Deferred candidates are deliberately NOT recorded. The directory holds far
-- more companies than a day's research budget, so the surplus has to come back
-- tomorrow, and the only thing making that happen is its absence from
-- discovery_seen.
WITH payload AS (
    SELECT $1::jsonb AS p
),
cand AS (
    SELECT
        c ->> 'source'                          AS source,
        c ->> 'external_id'                     AS external_id,
        lower(c ->> 'domain')::citext           AS domain,
        c ->> 'name'                            AS name,
        c ->> 'website'                         AS website,
        c ->> 'country'                         AS country,
        c ->> 'industry'                        AS industry,
        nullif(c ->> 'employee_count', '')::int AS employee_count,
        c ->> 'description'                     AS description,
        coalesce((c ->> 'priority')::int, 0)    AS priority,
        c -> 'evidence'                         AS evidence
    FROM payload, jsonb_array_elements(p -> 'candidates') AS c
    WHERE coalesce(btrim(c ->> 'domain'), '') <> ''
),
-- Anything decided on a previous run is gone for good, accepted or rejected.
fresh AS (
    SELECT c.*
    FROM cand c
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM discovery_seen s
        WHERE s.source = c.source AND s.external_id = c.external_id
    )
),
-- The same company can appear in both sources in the same run, and companies
-- has a unique domain. Keep the better-evidenced row. One per brand as well
-- (0027): officebrand.example and shop.officebrand.example arrived in the same run.
deduped AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (domain_brand(domain::text)) *
    FROM fresh
    ORDER BY domain_brand(domain::text), priority DESC, source, domain
),
classified AS (
    SELECT d.*,
        CASE
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM suppression_list sl
                WHERE sl.domain IS NOT NULL AND sl.domain = d.domain
            ) THEN 'suppressed'
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM companies co WHERE co.domain = d.domain
            ) THEN 'already_known'
            -- The same company on another domain (0027_draft_quality.sql):
            -- ba.shopbrand.example after shopbrand.example, shop.officebrand.example after officebrand.example.
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM companies co
                WHERE domain_brand(co.domain::text) = domain_brand(d.domain::text)
            ) THEN 'already_known'
            ELSE NULL
        END AS rejected
    FROM deduped d
),
-- The day's slots are shared out by ICP segment (0025_segment_allocation.sql):
-- each active segment first gets its discovery_share of the daily limit, then
-- whatever a segment could not use goes to the best remaining candidates of the
-- segments that have a share. A candidate in a segment with no share is never
-- taken, which is what keeps a source's easiest companies from filling the
-- table. regional_other has a share and no outreach: research reads those
-- companies and reclassifies them by what they do (segment_from_research).
lim AS (
    SELECT greatest(0, coalesce((SELECT (p ->> 'daily_limit')::int FROM payload), 25)) AS n
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT c.*, s.discovery_share,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.code ORDER BY c.priority DESC, c.domain) AS seg_rank
    FROM classified c
    JOIN icp_segments s ON s.code = segment_for(c.source, c.industry) AND s.discovery_share > 0
    WHERE c.rejected IS NULL
),
by_share AS (
    SELECT r.*
    FROM ranked r, lim
    WHERE r.seg_rank <= ceil(lim.n * r.discovery_share / 100.0)
),
accepted AS (
    (SELECT * FROM by_share ORDER BY priority DESC, domain LIMIT (SELECT n FROM lim))
    UNION ALL
    (SELECT r.* FROM ranked r
     WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM by_share b WHERE b.domain = r.domain)
     ORDER BY r.priority DESC, r.domain
     LIMIT greatest(0, (SELECT n FROM lim) - (SELECT count(*) FROM by_share)))
),
inserted AS (
    INSERT INTO companies (
        name, domain, website, country, industry,
        employee_count, description, source, status
    )
    SELECT
        left(btrim(a.name), 200), a.domain, a.website, a.country, a.industry,
        a.employee_count, left(a.description, 2000), a.source, 'new'
    FROM accepted a
    WHERE btrim(coalesce(a.name, '')) <> ''
    ON CONFLICT (domain) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id, domain, name
),
-- Why this company is in the table at all. Confidence is deliberately low:
-- being in a directory is not evidence of anything except being in a directory.
-- The exception says so in its evidence: Minimax's own list of the offices that
-- use it is evidence of exactly that (0029_minimax_directory.sql).
sig AS (
    INSERT INTO signals (company_id, signal_type, signal, source_url, confidence)
    SELECT i.id, 'other', left(a.evidence ->> 'note', 1000), a.evidence ->> 'url',
           coalesce((a.evidence ->> 'confidence')::numeric, 0.20)
    FROM inserted i
    JOIN accepted a ON a.domain = i.domain
    WHERE coalesce(btrim(a.evidence ->> 'note'), '') <> ''
    ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id
),
seen AS (
    INSERT INTO discovery_seen (source, external_id, domain, rejected)
    SELECT source, external_id, domain, rejected FROM classified WHERE rejected IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT source, external_id, domain, NULL FROM accepted
    ON CONFLICT (source, external_id) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM cand)                                      AS candidates_in,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM fresh)                                     AS not_seen_before,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM classified WHERE rejected = 'already_known') AS already_known,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM classified WHERE rejected = 'suppressed')    AS suppressed,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM accepted)                                  AS accepted,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM inserted)                                  AS companies_inserted,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM sig)                                       AS signals_inserted,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM seen)                                      AS seen_recorded,
    greatest(0, (SELECT count(*) FROM classified WHERE rejected IS NULL)
              - (SELECT count(*) FROM accepted))                     AS deferred_to_tomorrow,
    (SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('domain', domain, 'name', name)), '[]'::jsonb)
     FROM inserted)                                                  AS inserted_companies

-- One batched line a day. Discovery is not urgent and must never compete with
-- an approval request for attention; docs/telegram.md's rule is that an unmuted
-- channel is worth more than a complete one.
--
-- The dedup key carries the date, so a second run on the same day folds into
-- the first rather than sending twice.
SELECT *
FROM queue_notification(
    'system',
    'system:discovery:' || to_char(now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD'),
    'Discovery: ' || ($1::jsonb ->> 'companies_inserted') || ' new companies',
    'WF-01 added ' || ($1::jsonb ->> 'companies_inserted') || ' companies to the research queue.'
        || E'\n' || 'Considered ' || ($1::jsonb ->> 'candidates_in')
        || ', already known ' || ($1::jsonb ->> 'already_known')
        || ', suppressed ' || ($1::jsonb ->> 'suppressed')
        || ', left for tomorrow ' || ($1::jsonb ->> 'deferred_to_tomorrow') || '.'
        || E'\n\n'
        || coalesce(
             (SELECT string_agg('  ' || (e ->> 'domain') || '  ' || (e ->> 'name'), E'\n')
              FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb -> 'inserted_companies') AS e),
             '  (none)'),
    'batched',
    $1::jsonb,
    NULL,
    NULL,
    interval '12 hours'
)

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ candidates_in: $json.candidates_in, already_known: $json.already_known, suppressed: $json.suppressed, accepted: $json.accepted, companies_inserted: $json.companies_inserted, signals_inserted: $json.signals_inserted, deferred_to_tomorrow: $json.deferred_to_tomorrow, inserted_companies: $json.inserted_companies }) }}

nodes.name: Queue Discovery Alert
nodes.notes: Batched, not immediate. A discovery run is a fact for the morning report, not an interruption.

parameters.query:
-- OpenStreetMap comes from the snapshot WF-12 keeps, never from the network:
-- a morning when Overpass is down or refusing this IP costs nothing here.
--
-- One row per country in DISCOVERY_OSM_COUNTRIES, with origin 'none' for a
-- country WF-12 has not fetched yet. Always at least one row: an empty output
-- would stop the workflow here and YC and Hacker News would never be recorded.
-- With OSM switched off the row carries no country.
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
c AS (
    SELECT iso, ord
    FROM p, unnest(string_to_array(upper(regexp_replace(p.j ->> 'countries', '\s', '', 'g')), ',')) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(iso, ord)
    WHERE iso ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'
)
SELECT c.iso,
       s.payload                                               AS data,
       CASE WHEN s.country IS NULL THEN 'none' ELSE 'snapshot' END AS origin,
       s.fetched_at                                            AS snapshot_at,
       CASE WHEN s.country IS NULL THEN 'no snapshot yet (WF-12)' END AS problem
FROM c
LEFT JOIN osm_snapshot s ON s.country = c.iso
UNION ALL
SELECT NULL, NULL, 'disabled', NULL, NULL
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM c)
ORDER BY 1;

-- Public directories, from the snapshot make minimax-refresh keeps
-- (0029_minimax_directory.sql). One row per directory and country. Always at
-- least one row: an empty output would stop the workflow here and no source
-- would be recorded.
SELECT d.source, d.country AS iso, d.url, d.entries::text AS data, d.fetched_at AS snapshot_at
FROM directory_snapshot d
UNION ALL
SELECT NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM directory_snapshot)
ORDER BY 1, 2;
